                    ### Question
                    A thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain has been isolated at a retirement home. Many of the elderly had been infected with this strain and are experiencing shingles. Which of the following would be the best antiviral agent to treat this population?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Acyclovir
opb. Famciclovir
opc. Ganciclovir
opd. Cidofovir
ope. Amantadine

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the case of a thymidine kinase-deficient varicella-zoster virus strain, acyclovir and famciclovir are ineffective as they require thymidine kinase for activation. Ganciclovir, although activated by a different kinase, and cidofovir, which does not require viral kinase for activation, remain effective options. Amantadine is not effective as it targets influenza viruses, not varicella-zoster. The evidence path confirming the interaction between thymidine kinase and acyclovir supports the ineffectiveness of acyclovir in this scenario. Given the effectiveness and the activation pathways, cidofovir and ganciclovir are the best antiviral agents for treating this population.
